A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same authors' editing framework and ALE-Bench, despite the revised title and organization. Their complete main texts, appendices, tables, figures, and equations support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative and qualitative evaluations on ALE-Bench and PIE-Bench, component and EOS ablations, and self-attention schedule experiments.

after.justification: v4 retains original benchmark evaluations and ablations and additionally reports runtime measurements and qualitative ETS comparisons.

M1.justification: The ORE/RGB-CAM/BB framework remains. However, v1's ORE algorithm explicitly constructs embeddings by replacing base-prompt spans and zeroing other objects, whereas v4 Section 3.2 describes independently padded object embeddings without explaining equivalent alignment and zeroing. The PDFs do not resolve whether this reflects a procedural change or an incomplete rewrite.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ALE-Bench's 20 images, 3,000 edits, five editing types, and one-to-three-object scenarios, plus the same four compatible PIE-Bench editing types. PIE-Bench was already evaluated in v1's appendix. Added ETS examples remain within existing task coverage.

E2.justification: P2P, MasaCtrl, FPE, and InfEdit remain the benchmark comparators. v4 adds qualitative comparisons against End Token Substitution (ETS), including the direct ETS-versus-ALE examples in Figure 10. This does not establish evaluation of the complete ToMe method.

E3.justification: v4 adds runtime evaluation in seconds per edit on an RTX 6000 Ada and ETS comparisons with and without cross-attention masking. The documented benchmark construction, leakage metrics, 15 inference steps, and edit-specific schedule values remain unchanged. Omitted common settings do not establish that retained experiments used different backbones or were rerun.

E4.justification: v4 adds ETS case studies and attention-map comparisons testing whether object-wise embeddings and spatial masking resolve EOS entanglement (Figures 3 and 10). Existing EOS-replacement, component, schedule-sensitivity, and backbone-failure analyses are largely retained, including their appendix evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Both retain ten random edit prompts per benchmark combination. The new average-runtime table does not disclose repeated-run counts or introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Reported ALE-Bench scores receive mostly small revisions: P2P's aggregate external leakage changes from 21.48 to 21.52, and ALE's two-object internal leakage from 15.31 to 15.42. Rankings broadly persist; ALE's aggregate row, quantitative ablations, and PIE-Bench scores remain unchanged. v4 adds ETS qualitative findings and runtime results, including 4.31 seconds for ALE versus 5.41 for InfEdit.

T1.justification: The task's leakage categories and CLIP-based leakage-score definitions retain their mathematical substance. No new theoretical assumptions, propositions, proofs, or substantive derivations are introduced. Removing generic diffusion preliminaries and rewriting method notation primarily changes exposition.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain training-free multi-object editing using ORE, RGB-CAM, and BB; identifying embedding-related leakage; and introducing ALE-Bench with two leakage metrics. Naming the framework ALE and emphasizing EOS entanglement sharpen the presentation without materially changing these claims.

C2.justification: v4 explains why ETS can retain noun-to-noun confusion despite removing attribute descriptors, and why spatial masking alone cannot remove entangled EOS semantics. It also interprets runtime differences through inversion mechanisms and expands discussion of why non-rigid editing would require different leakage definitions and metrics. Dataset-size and backbone limitations already appeared in v1.

D1.justification: Reproducibility documentation is substantially replaced: v1's detailed ORE/RGB-CAM algorithms and notation appendix give way to an overall pipeline algorithm. Explicit common-LCM, 768-by-768 resolution, embedding-dimension, and evaluation-mask refinement disclosures are omitted. v4 adds a project-page link, runtime hardware information, and clarification that ORE-only ablations use the base embedding.

R1.justification: v4 substantially refocuses related work from broad diffusion generation and controllability toward editing and embedding entanglement. It replaces the detailed RPG/SPDiffusion positioning with discussion of ToMe/ETS, adds relevant approaches such as Attend-and-Excite and SynGen, and explicitly contrasts ALE-Bench with LoMOE-Bench. This changes the substantive account of the nearest prior work.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, problem analysis, method narrative, and related work are extensively rewritten and reorganized. v4 introduces ALE terminology, distinguishes TEL/TIL from TELS/TILS, expands the dual-branch explanation, brings limitations into the main text, and reorganizes the appendices.

P2.justification: v4 moves and redesigns the opening comparison, redraws the pipeline, adds leakage and ETS visualizations, and replaces the module-level algorithm displays with a complete pipeline algorithm. Benchmark examples gain separate mask displays, tables are restyled and reordered, and retained qualitative grids and failure examples are relocated.

improvement.justification: Clearer exposition, ETS comparisons, and runtime evidence offer benefits, but reduced implementation detail and new inconsistencies prevent a reliable net judgment. v4 Section 3.1 and Algorithm 1 specify conflicting injection intervals. Its balanced breakdowns imply aggregate ALE TELS of approximately 16.10, while Table 1 retains 16.03; v1's corresponding aggregation was consistent. Together with the unresolved ORE construction change, these issues offset the identifiable gains in clarity and evidence.
